anchor: belted Billy rolling along the upper gun deck
note: Belted: wearing a belt. Billy walks with a sailor’s rolling gait.
A broadside is all the guns on one side firing at once. Here, a burst of jokes.
Hyperion was a Titan of Greek myth, father of the sun god, so a figure of dazzling beauty.

anchor: his eyes strangely suffused with incipient feverish tears
note: Suffused: spread over, filled. Incipient: just beginning.
A phrase from the prophecy of Isaiah: “a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief,” later applied to Jesus.
source: The Bible (King James Version), Isaiah 53:3, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/10

note: Yearning: a deep longing, here of Claggart for Billy.
Evanescence: something that quickly fades away.
Immitigable: impossible to soften or lessen, hard and fixed.

anchor: the glittering dental satire of a Guise
note: A cruel smile that shows the teeth. The Guise were a French family known for ruthless intrigue.

anchor: a spark from an anvil in a dusk smithy
note: Smithy: a blacksmith’s shop. An anvil is the iron block on which he hammers metal.
Caprices: sudden whims. The pit suggests hell.
Thews: muscles and sinews, signs of bodily strength.

anchor: an admonition of the proximity of the malign
note: Admonition: a warning. Malign: evil, harmful.
A warning against a man whose words are too smooth to trust.

anchor: Two minor officers—the Armorer and Captain of the Hold
note: The armourer kept the ship’s weapons in repair. The captain of the hold looked after the cargo space below.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Armourer”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000; W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Captain of the hold”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

note: The yeoman guarded the ship’s stores. The apothecary was the ship’s medical helper.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Yeoman”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

note: Precocity: developing early. A young man already skilled in dishonesty.
Ignominiously: shamefully. Baffled: defeated, left puzzled.
Disaffection: discontent with those in authority, leading to revolt.
Monomania: an obsession with a single idea.
Subterranean: underground. A fire burning below the surface.
